pages.title: Installation
pages.description: Install AnimateIcons via the @animateicons/react npm package, the animateicons CLI, the shadcn CLI, or the MCP server for AI agents.
pages.content:
# Installation

Pick whichever path fits your setup. They all ship the same icons and the same API. The difference is whether you depend on the package or copy the source into your project.

## npm package

**Recommended** Best for most apps. One install, all
1170 icons available.

#### 1. Install the package

Use any package manager. `motion` is bundled.

- `npm install @animateicons/react`
- `pnpm add @animateicons/react`
- `yarn add @animateicons/react`
- `bun add @animateicons/react`

#### 2. Import an icon

Lucide and Huge are exposed as scoped subpaths because some icon names overlap (`HeartIcon`, `CopyIcon`, etc.).

```tsx title="Example.tsx"
import { EyeIcon } from "@animateicons/react/huge"

export default function Example() {
	return <EyeIcon size={24} color="#f45b48" />
}
```

> **Tip:** Icons animate on hover out of the box, no extra wiring. Pass `size`, `color`, or any prop to customize.

#### Next.js App Router

Import each icon from its own file. Importing from the main package loads every icon: 918 kB of client JavaScript, compared with 71 kB for one icon.

```tsx title="Example.tsx"
import { BellRingIcon } from "@animateicons/react/lucide/bell-ring-icon"
import { HeartIcon } from "@animateicons/react/huge/heart-icon"
```

The path is the icon's file name, so `BellRingIcon` becomes `bell-ring-icon`. These paths only work with ESM imports. If you use `require()`, import from the main package.

## Prefer to copy the source?

If you'd rather own the icon files instead of depending on the package, use the [shadcn CLI](https://animateicons.in/icons/docs/shadcn) or the first-party [animateicons CLI](https://animateicons.in/icons/docs/cli). Using an AI coding agent? The [MCP server](https://animateicons.in/icons/docs/mcp) lets it add icons for you.

Once icons are in your project, head to [Usage](https://animateicons.in/icons/docs/usage) for styling, the imperative API, and full types.

pages.title: Usage
pages.description: Style AnimateIcons with color, className, and duration, trigger animations imperatively with a ref, and see the full prop and handle types.
pages.content:
# Usage

Every icon shares the same small API: a few style props and an optional ref handle. The examples below use `EyeIcon`, but they apply to every icon in both libraries.

## Styling

Every icon strokes `currentColor`, so it inherits the surrounding text color. You can also pass `color`, `className`, or use the `duration` and `isAnimated` props to control playback.

```tsx title="Styling.tsx"
// Color - sets currentColor inline
<EyeIcon color="#f45b48" />

// Tailwind utility - works because icons stroke="currentColor"

<EyeIcon className="text-primary" />

// Speed - duration is a multiplier (lower = faster)

<EyeIcon duration={0.6} />

// Disable hover animation

<EyeIcon isAnimated={false} />
```

> **Tip:** Because icons stroke `currentColor`, they inherit color from any parent, so a Tailwind `text-*` class or a CSS `color` is all you need to theme them.

## Imperative API

Need to trigger an animation from a parent, on click, on focus, or programmatically? Pass a ref. Each icon exports its own `*Handle` type.

```tsx title="Demo.tsx"
"use client"

import { useRef } from "react"
import { EyeIcon, type EyeIconHandle } from "@/components/ui/eye"

export default function Demo() {
	const ref = useRef<EyeIconHandle>(null)

    return (
    	<button
    		onMouseEnter={() => ref.current?.startAnimation()}
    		onMouseLeave={() => ref.current?.stopAnimation()}
    	>
    		<EyeIcon ref={ref} size={28} />
    	</button>
    )

}
```

> **Note:** The ref handle only works in Client Components. Add `"use client"` to the file that calls `startAnimation()`.

> **Tip:** Use `useIconHover` to play icons on hover or click without writing the handlers yourself. See the [Hover helper](https://animateicons.in/icons/docs/examples/hover-helper).

## Props & types

```ts title="Types"
interface IconProps {
	size?: number
	color?: string
	className?: string
	duration?: number
	isAnimated?: boolean
	onMouseEnter?: (e: React.MouseEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => void
	onMouseLeave?: (e: React.MouseEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => void
	style?: React.CSSProperties
}

interface IconHandle {
startAnimation: () => void
stopAnimation: () => void
}
```

> **Note:** Animations respect the OS-level **Reduce Motion** preference, so no extra setup is required.

pages.title: shadcn CLI
pages.description: Add AnimateIcons to your project with the shadcn CLI. Each icon is copied into your codebase as a single editable file from the AnimateIcons registry.
pages.content:
# shadcn CLI

Use this if you want each icon copied into your codebase as a single file you can edit.

#### 1. Set up shadcn

If your project doesn't have shadcn yet, follow the [shadcn installation guide](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/installation) first.

#### 2. Add an icon

Browse the [Lucide](https://animateicons.in/icons/lucide) or [Huge](https://animateicons.in/icons/huge) gallery, click any tile to copy its install command, or replace `lu-eye` below with the icon you want.

- `npx shadcn@latest add @animateicons/lu-eye`
- `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @animateicons/lu-eye`
- `bunx --bun shadcn@latest add @animateicons/lu-eye`

The icon lands at `components/ui/<name>-icon.tsx`.

#### 3. Import and use

```tsx title="Example.tsx"
import { EyeIcon } from "@/components/ui/eye-icon"

export default function Example() {
	return <EyeIcon size={24} color="#f45b48" />
}
```

pages.title: animateicons CLI
pages.description: Copy AnimateIcons into your project with the first-party animateicons CLI. Add, search, and browse icons without leaving the terminal.
pages.content:
# animateicons CLI

The fastest way to copy icons into your project. Same result as the shadcn CLI, but a first-party command instead of a registry URL.

#### 1. Add an icon

```bash title="Terminal"
npx animateicons add eye

# add several at once, or use the lu-/hu- prefixed id

npx animateicons add eye bell-ring user
```

Prefer a short command? Install the CLI globally and an `animateicons` binary is added to your PATH:

```bash title="Terminal"
npm i -g animateicons
animateicons add eye
```

Icons land at `components/icons/<name>.tsx` (override with `--dir`). The CLI also prints the `motion` install command for your package manager.

> **Note:** Copied icons import `cn` from `@/lib/utils`. If your project isn't shadcn-based, pass `--with-utils` and the CLI scaffolds a minimal helper for you.

#### 2. Browse without leaving the terminal

```bash title="Terminal"
npx animateicons search notification
npx animateicons list --library huge
npx animateicons info eye
```

Or open the interactive dashboard to search, multi-select, and add icons live in your terminal:

```bash title="Terminal"
npx animateicons browse
```

#### 3. Import and use

```tsx title="Example.tsx"
import { EyeIcon } from "@/components/icons/eye"

export default function Example() {
	return <EyeIcon size={24} color="#f45b48" />
}
```

pages.title: MCP Server
pages.description: Connect the @animateicons/mcp Model Context Protocol server so AI coding agents like Claude Code and Cursor can search and add animated React icons for you.
pages.content:
# MCP server

`@animateicons/mcp` is a [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server. Connect it to an AI coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, and others), and the agent can search the AnimateIcons catalog and drop animated icons straight into your project, no copy-pasting.

## What it can do

Once connected, your agent gets five tools:

- `search_icons`: fuzzy-search the catalog by name, keyword, or category.
- `get_icon`: return an icon's component source plus a ready-to-paste import (read-only).
- `add_icon`: write an icon's component file into your project (default `components/icons/`).
- `get_docs`: read these docs, including the props, the ref handle, the `useIconHover` hook and the examples. Without a page it lists them.
- `list_libraries`: list the libraries and how many icons each has.

## Claude Code

Register the server in one command:

```bash title="Terminal"
claude mcp add animateicons -- npx -y @animateicons/mcp
```

> **Tip:** Restart Claude Code (or reload your editor window) after adding the server so it registers the new tools.

Then just ask, and the agent picks the right tool:

```tsx title="In your editor"
// Then just ask your agent in plain language:
//   "add a notification bell icon"
//
// → it calls search_icons, picks bell-ring, then add_icon
//   and writes components/icons/bell-ring.tsx for you.
```

## Cursor & other clients

Add the server to your MCP config (e.g. `.cursor/mcp.json` or `.mcp.json`):

```json title=".mcp.json"
{
	"mcpServers": {
		"animateicons": {
			"command": "npx",
			"args": ["-y", "@animateicons/mcp"]
		}
	}
}
```

## Requirements

> **Note:** Icons written by `add_icon` import `cn` from `@/lib/utils` (the shadcn convention) and require the [motion](https://motion.dev) package at runtime.

Prefer the terminal? The [CLI](https://animateicons.in/icons/docs/cli) does the same thing with `npx animateicons add`.
